question: The chord of a circle is equal to its radius. The angle (in degrees) subtended by this chord at any point on the minor arc of the circle is:
solution:
**Given:**

The chords of a circle = radius of the circle

**Concept used:**

The angle of an equilateral triangle = 60°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be2bdeec80d53e4a8ce034529d6fb1351816e3b4c859c64d2ad2b4584cf14852.png] 

In the figure:

OD = OE = radius

DE = OD = OE

So, △DOE is an equilateral triangle.

∠DOE = 60°

⇒ ∠DQE = (∠DOE/2)

⇒ 60/2 = 30°

DQEP is a cyclic quadrilateral.

∠DQE + ∠DPE = 180°

⇒ 30 + ∠DPE = 180

⇒ ∠DPE = 180 - 30

⇒ ∠DPE = 150°

**∴ The correct answer is 150°.**
